newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RSL takes 51 pct of Israel's Delta Three.
newsitem.headline: RSL takes 51 pct of Israel's Delta Three.

text.p: U.S. telecoms firm RSL Communications Ltd has bought a 51 percent stake in Israel's Delta Three Inc, a provider of telephone services over the Internet, for $10 million, Delta Three said on Monday.
Delta Three President and CEO Elie Wurtman said RSL, part of a group of companies owned by cosmetics heir Ronald Lauder, had paid $5 million in cash and $5 million in services for the stake.

"RSL was one of Delta Three's first clients going back about seven months. We're the first companies to prove the commercial feasibility of telecommunications traffic over the internet," Wurtman told Reuters.
Both companies are closely held. Delta Three's remaining 49 percent is owned by the Jerusalem-based firm's management.
Delta Three's internet telephony services allow subscribers to make real-time long distance phone calls at local rates from a regular telephone without use of computer.
"You call to a Delta Three server where the voice signal is converted, transmitted over the net to another Delta Three server and then converted back into voice for the end user," Wurtman said.
Wurtman said Delta Three was looking to go public on Nasdaq in the United States during the next year. "We're actively looking to do that somewhere in the next nine to 12 months."
He said Delta Three offered its services on a retail basis in the United States and Europe and had a presence in South America, Japan and Russia.
